name: MOMENTUM OS
tagline: A local-first personal productivity OS for students that puts tasks, habits, focus sprints, notes and goals on an illustrated desk.
problem: Students juggling assignments, internships, hackathons and habits usually spread them across several apps and lose track of what matters today. Momentum OS keeps all of it in one workspace stored in the browser, with a light game layer of XP, levels and badges to keep going.
how: On first launch a sleeping cat named Sparky lies on the keyboard; moving it unlocks a TODAY I WILL notepad where you write the day's tasks.
GO TO MY DESK opens the Home Base: pinned tasks on a corkboard, a to-do pad, momentum and urgency gauges, a focus timer, a wall calendar and life-area plants.
A bottom tray opens rooms for Overview, Tasks, Habits, Calendar, Focus, Notes, Charts, Goals, Awards and Settings.
Data is kept in IndexedDB through Dexie and Zustand, with optional Supabase sign-in.
The AI Assistant drawer turns natural-language commands into structured tasks or assignments and answers questions about deadlines.
A Classic V2.5 sidebar mode offers fuller dashboards such as the Momentum Overview and Analytics charts.
features: Interactive Sleeping Cat onboarding with a first-tasks notepad
Cozy Marker Desk home base with pinned tasks, gauges, calendar and focus timer
Task list with quick add, due dates and completion that awards XP
Habit engine with quick add, daily check-ins, streaks and a knitted scarf view
XP, coins and levels: tasks and habit check-ins award XP and the level rises at the XP threshold
Achievements such as First Task Completed and Habit Weaver
AI Assistant drawer for natural-language task capture and deadline questions
Classic V2.5 sidebar OS with Momentum Overview, Analytics and Recharts charts
ai: The AI Assistant parses commands such as Remind me to submit my OS assignment next Tuesday at 5 pm into a structured draft with date, time, priority and energy level, and answers questions about pending deadlines.
It calls Groq through the /api/ai route when GROQ_API_KEY is set and otherwise falls back to a built-in local heuristic parser.

stack.frontend: Next.js 16 App Router, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion, Recharts
stack.backend: Next.js route handlers for AI and transcription
stack.data: Zustand store persisted to IndexedDB with Dexie; optional Supabase
stack.ai: Groq SDK with a local heuristic fallback provider

notes: Ran locally as a production build with no env vars, so it used guest mode with local IndexedDB storage and no Supabase. The app ships no sample data, so the tasks, habits and note were typed into the real UI. No Groq key was set, so the AI Assistant replies come from the app's built-in local heuristic fallback (the /api/ai route answers 400 and the client falls back, which shows once as a console network error). The earlier capture hit runtime errors because the desk components called addXP and toggleHabitCheckIn, which the store does not define. This capture was made after two small local fixes in the repo (not pushed): the desk now calls the store's awardXP and logHabitCompletion and reads check-in state from completionHistory, and the sign out dialog calls the auth store's logout instead of the undefined signOut. With those fixes habit boxes check, streaks and XP update, and the level rose from L1 to L2 at 1000 XP after 15 habit check-ins and a task. To reach Level 2 in a short recording, fifteen habits were added and checked in the UI, so the XP total reflects that scripted use. No console errors appeared on the screens shown. Not exercised: the Goals and project milestone controls (the guest data has no goals or projects), the deadline risk dialogs (the store has no risk data), and focus sprint completion (a full 50 minutes). The Overview tile for focus minutes always reads 0 because it reads a field the timer state does not have. The repo has many TypeScript type errors that Next.js does not check at build time.
